title: Accounts Receivable Rule: Household Utility Balance, Payment Application and Carry to Final Accounting
content:
# Household Utility Balance — Utility Services Program

**Rule.** A household's utility balance under the Utility Services Program is the sum of the balance due over all its utility accounts, including an account in final billing after a transfer. A payment is applied to the account it is made on, oldest bill line first; a credit balance on one account is applied to the open balance of the household's other utility account before any refund. At final accounting the remaining utility balance of every account tied to the lease is carried into the final account statement under the Security Deposit Account charter, and each account is closed once its final bill has been issued and its balance paid or carried there. Unpaid utility charges never lead to an interruption of service — Larkspur never disconnects or restricts a utility for non-payment — and never incur a late fee under the Utility Services Program.

## The rule, point by point

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Which accounts make up the household's utility balance? | Every utility account of the household, including one in final billing after a transfer. |
| Which account does a payment reduce? | The account it is made on. |
| Which line of that account does a payment reach first? | The oldest bill line. |
| What happens to a credit balance on one account? | It is applied to the open balance of the household's other utility account before any refund. |
| What happens to the remaining balance at final accounting? | It is carried into the final account statement under the Security Deposit Account charter, for every account tied to the lease. |
| When is each account closed? | Once its final bill has been issued and its balance has been paid or carried into the final account statement. |
| Can service be interrupted or a late fee charged for unpaid utility charges? | No. Larkspur never disconnects or restricts a utility for non-payment, and no late fee is incurred under this program. |

*Worked example (hypothetical balances):* a household that has transferred holds an account in final billing with $40.00 due and a new active account with $65.00 due. The household's utility balance is $105.00. A payment of $30.00 made on the new account reduces only that account, to $35.00, starting with its oldest bill line; the account in final billing still shows $40.00.
